title: Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016
summary: Pakistan's principal federal statute on offences involving information systems and data, related investigation and evidence-gathering powers, service-provider duties, and online-content controls.
key_provisions: Creates offences involving unauthorized access, copying or interference with systems and data, identity information, interception, cyberstalking, and specified forms of online content.
Requires service providers to retain specified traffic data for at least one year and provide it when supported by a court warrant.
Provides procedures for preservation, search, seizure, disclosure, real-time collection, confidentiality, prosecution, trial, and international cooperation.

title: Criminal Laws (Amendment) Act, 2023
summary: An amending act that added child-focused online offences, cyberbullying provisions, investigation procedures, and victim protections to PECA and made related changes to evidence and criminal law.
key_provisions: Adds PECA offences concerning online grooming, child sexual exploitation, and use of information systems for kidnapping, abduction, or trafficking of a minor.
Adds a cyberbullying offence and a route for a minor, through a guardian, to seek removal or blocking of the relevant content.
Adds investigation timelines, remand rules, victim and witness protections, in-camera trial provisions, and a victim-support mechanism.

title: Prevention of Electronic Crimes (Amendment) Act, 2025
summary: An amendment to PECA that creates a new social-media regulatory structure, revises online-content provisions, adds a false-information offence, and assigns PECA investigations to the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency.
key_provisions: Provides for a Social Media Protection and Regulatory Authority, a Social Media Complaint Council, and a Social Media Protection Tribunal.
Establishes enlistment and complaint-handling provisions for social media platforms and defines categories of unlawful or offensive online content.
Adds an offence concerning intentional dissemination of false or fake information and substitutes the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency as the investigation agency.

title: Citizens Protection (Against Online Harm) Rules, 2020
summary: A repealed ruleset that established a national coordinator and imposed content-removal, local-presence, data-disclosure, and enforcement obligations on social media companies.
key_provisions: Required notified unlawful content to be removed or disabled within twenty-four hours, or six hours in an emergency.
Required covered companies to register, establish a local office and focal person, and establish database servers in Pakistan.
Authorized service blocking and financial penalties for non-compliance.

title: Removal and Blocking of Unlawful Online Content (Procedure, Oversight and Safeguards) Rules, 2020
summary: A repealed ruleset that prescribed a Pakistan Telecommunication Authority process for complaints, removal or blocking orders, platform obligations, review, and appeal concerning unlawful online content.
key_provisions: Established complaint and hearing procedures for Pakistan Telecommunication Authority decisions on unlawful online content.
Set compliance requirements for service providers and social media companies.
Provided review within the Authority and a subsequent appeal route to the High Court.

title: Removal and Blocking of Unlawful Online Content (Procedure, Oversight and Safeguards) Rules, 2021
summary: Rules governing Pakistan Telecommunication Authority complaints, notices, hearings, removal or blocking directions, platform obligations, enforcement, review, and appeal under PECA's online-content provisions.
key_provisions: Provides a complaint process and generally requires an opportunity to be heard before a removal or blocking order.
Sets a forty-eight-hour compliance period for directions, with a shorter period for emergency cases.
Provides for review by the Authority and appeal to the High Court, and repeals both federal online-content rulesets issued in 2020.

title: Personal Data Protection Bill, 2023
issuing_body: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
summary: A federal draft bill proposing rules for collection, processing, use, disclosure, security, and cross-border transfer of personal data, together with data-subject rights and a national data-protection commission.
key_provisions: Sets proposed obligations for lawful and fair processing, consent, purpose limitation, security, and breach notification.
Proposes rights including access, correction, erasure, grievance redress, portability, and protections concerning automated processing.
Proposes a National Commission for Personal Data Protection with complaint, enforcement, and penalty functions.

title: Electronic Transactions Ordinance, 2002
summary: Pakistan's framework for legal recognition of electronic documents, communications, signatures, and certification services; its original privacy and information-system damage offences were omitted by PECA in 2016.
key_provisions: Recognizes electronic documents, records, communications, and signatures and sets rules for attribution, acknowledgement, and retention.
Establishes the Electronic Certification Accreditation Council and a framework for certification service providers.
Permits regulations addressing privacy and protection of certification-service subscriber data; PECA omitted the Ordinance's former sections 36 and 37.

title: Investigation for Fair Trial Act, 2013
summary: A federal statute regulating warrants for surveillance and interception in investigations of scheduled offences, including executive authorization, High Court oversight, service-provider cooperation, and controls on use of intercepted material.
key_provisions: Requires an authorized officer to obtain ministerial permission before applying to a High Court judge for a surveillance or interception warrant.
Directs the judge to consider evidentiary need and privacy interference when deciding whether and how to issue a warrant.
Provides for review, complaints concerning misuse, confidentiality, admissibility, and offences for unauthorized surveillance or misuse of intercepted material.

title: Pakistan Telecommunication (Re-organization) Act, 1996
summary: The foundational statute for Pakistan's telecommunications institutions and licensing system, including the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority, universal-service funding, right-of-way rules, national-security powers, and sector appeals.
key_provisions: Establishes the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority and assigns it licensing, regulatory, consumer-protection, competition, and universal-service functions.
Establishes the Universal Service Fund for access in unserved, underserved, rural, and remote areas.
Authorizes specified interception and service-priority measures for national-security purposes and provides for a Telecommunication Appellate Tribunal.

title: Public & Private Right of Way Policy Directive
summary: A federal directive to facilitate deployment and maintenance of telecommunications infrastructure across public and private rights of way.
key_provisions: Sets a policy framework for right-of-way permissions and fee determination for telecommunications infrastructure.
Addresses dispute resolution, infrastructure protection, sharing of rights of way, and common service corridors.
Directs the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority on implementation under the telecommunications statute.

title: Telecommunications Policy 2015
summary: A national policy for universal, affordable, and quality telecommunications through competitive markets, covering broadband expansion, spectrum, competition, convergence, satellite services, and universal service.
key_provisions: Sets universal access, affordability, quality, and competition as central policy objectives.
Provides policy direction on spectrum strategy and sharing, broadband infrastructure, satellite communications, and over-the-top services.
Reframes universal service to support broadband demand and connectivity in rural and underserved areas.

title: Universal Service Fund Rules, 2006
summary: Rules for administering and managing Pakistan's Universal Service Fund and its programs for extending telecommunications and broadband access to unserved and underserved areas.
key_provisions: Defines the Fund's governance through a policy committee, fund secretariat, and state-owned Universal Service Fund company.
Provides for competitive allocation of subsidies and projects serving unserved and underserved areas.
Sets budgeting, contribution, disbursement, contracting, monitoring, and reporting arrangements for universal-service projects.

title: USF Rules Amendments 2023
summary: Amendments to the Universal Service Fund Rules that revise definitions, governance, board composition, and company budgeting and reporting arrangements.
key_provisions: Reconstitutes the Universal Service Fund company board with government, industry, executive, and independent members.
Specifies independent legal, financial, and telecommunications or information-technology expertise on the board.
Updates definitions and selected fund, company, budget, and reporting provisions in the 2006 rules.

title: National Broadband Policy 2021, Consultation Draft v3.0
issuing_body: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
summary: A consultation draft proposing a national framework for universal, affordable high-speed internet, digital inclusion, infrastructure expansion, service quality, market development, digital trust, and technology evolution.
key_provisions: Proposes national broadband targets and measures to reduce access gaps in unserved and underserved areas.
Proposes infrastructure-sharing, fiberization, spectrum, right-of-way, affordability, and quality-of-service measures.
Organizes implementation around inclusivity and accessibility, usability and market enablement, digital trust, and transformation and evolution.
